newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit rangebound as profit-taking caps dlr rise.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit rangebound as profit-taking caps dlr rise.

text.p: * Ringgit moves in tight range amid cautious dealing
* U.S. hedge funds seen taking profit at 2.5650
* Dollar seen pulling back after failure to scale 2.5700
* Interbank activity slows ahead of holiday in Malaysia
The ringgit was trapped in a narrow range in early Asian trading after dollar gains were capped by U.S. hedge funds taking profit, dealers said.
"U.S. hedge funds were seen taking profit at 2.5650 this morning," said a European bank dealer in Kuala Lumpur. "The market is long dollars and this will slow down its rise."
Trading was thin with interbank activity slowing ahead of a holiday in Malaysia on Thursday.
At 0200 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5625/35 to a dollar after opening around 2.5650/60. It closed at 2.5580/10 in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday.
Dealers said the dollar risks a pullback to 2.5500 after its failure to scale the 2.5700 high overnight. The dollar/ringgit hit 2.5700, its strongest level since October 1994, in New York on Monday.
But dealers said the ringgit's undertone remains bearish due to a change in stance by central Bank Negara.

Acting Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Tuesday that Malaysia would allow the exchange rate to be determined by market forces and that the country did not favour a high interest rate regime.
Anwar's comments baffled the market after Bank Negara governor Ahmad Mohamed Don said last week that interest rates would stay high to curb speculation in the ringgit.

The statement was also interpreted that the authorities were willing to tolerate further ringgit weakness, dealers said, adding that they did not discount the possibility of funds pushing dollar/ringgit towards 2.6000.
